newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa may be released this week - doctors.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa may be released this week - doctors.

text.p: Mother Teresa, recovering rapidly after heart surgery and pneumonia, may be released from hospital this week, doctors and medical officials said on Wednesday.
"We may release her in a day or two," Dr Tarun Praharaj, a member of the team treating the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun at Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre, told Reuters.
"That will depend on her progress. She is stable," Praharaj added. "We are observing her."
A clinic official told reporters he hoped the missionary would be released by Friday.
"Mother Teresa appears to be out of danger... She is much better and we may release her by Friday," clinic administrator A.K. Chatterjee told reporters.
"Physicians are very happy with her improvement," the hospital said in a regular update on Mother Teresa's condition.
"The poor people need us so much," it quoted Mother Teresa as saying in response to the news.
During her stay in hospital, Mother Teresa has implored doctors to let her return to her work with the poor and sick which has earned her the title the "Saint of the Gutters".
"Mother was very happy to hear this morning that she may be going home soon," the bulletin added.

It quoted Dr Patricia Aubanel, an American member of the panel, as saying: "If Mother Teresa continues making progress in the next 24 hours, Mother will be going home soon and continue her recovery there."
Mother Teresa was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989. She had surgery last month to unblock two coronary arteries, the third such operation in five years.
But an irregular heartbeat and long-standing lung and kidney problems delayed her recovery. Twice in the past week doctors have given her a mild electric shock to regulate her heartbeat.
Bronchitis, which worried the doctors because it has dogged Mother Teresa from her earliest years, had finally cleared up, the bulletin said.
"Mother Teresa's pulmonary status is improving, and the infection has been cleared," the bulletin said, adding that her heart condition remained stable and the rhythm regular.
An earlier bulletin had said that Mother Teresa's condition had improved overnight.
"Mother Teresa is better today. She had a good sleep last night. She had her morning tea around 0730 and morning prayer at 0815 hrs," the bulletin said.
Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda visited the 1979 Nobel peace prize winner in hospital on Tuesday and gave her a get-well bouquet of roses.

Mother Teresa's doctors have said they hope she will be well enough to celebrate Christmas with her colleagues in the order, but have warned that her recovery will be lengthy and she may never be as active as before.
